idiom_name: translation-unit static instance + accessor; pthread_once for lazy construction
implementation_notes: C has no classes and no enforced uniqueness: the pattern collapses to a file-scope object with static storage duration as the sole instance, an opaque handle in the header, and an accessor returning a pointer to it, with lazy construction guarded by pthread_once (POSIX) or call_once from <threads.h> (C11). Nothing in the language replaces the structure - the private-constructor trick does not exist, and both the accessor and the once-flag are hand-written - while the uniqueness itself comes free from internal linkage. Keep the instance static in the .c file and hand out a pointer to const; passing the pointer into the functions that need it (dependency injection) still beats global access everywhere except genuine device/configuration cases.
pitfalls: An automatic or merely zero-initialised once_control is undefined behaviour: it must be a static object initialised with PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT (or ONCE_FLAG_INIT for call_once).
Static storage duration gives a zeroed object, not a constructed one: any code that reads the instance without going through the accessor sees an uninitialised struct.
Returning a non-const pointer lets callers mutate shared state without synchronisation; return const struct * and expose mutating operations as functions.
Nothing stops a second definition in another translation unit: keep the instance static (internal linkage) and never publish the struct layout.
forked children inherit a copy of the instance, so a 'singleton' connection or lock is duplicated after fork().

variants.name: C11 <threads.h> call_once
variants.implementation_notes: On toolchains that provide C11 <threads.h> (mandated by POSIX.1-2024 but absent from MSVC and from several embedded libc implementations) the standard once_flag/call_once pair replaces the POSIX call while the static instance and accessor stay the same. Prefer it when portability across C11 implementations matters more than the widest libc coverage, and note that <pthread.h> remains the recommended interface on POSIX systems.
pitfalls: <threads.h> is optional in ISO C: check __STDC_NO_THREADS__ before including it, and fall back to pthread_once where the header does not exist.
A recursive call_once on the same flag never returns: the initialiser must not re-enter the accessor.
